note: Evidence shard for the manufacturing/reliability workstream (D15-D18). Every URL below was requested with web_fetch on 2026-11-02 and returned HTTP 200 unless the limitations say otherwise. Only official standards-body, official EU and classification-society pages are recorded. The standard TEXTS were not purchased or read; the records describe catalogue metadata and scope statements, not clause-level requirements. No laboratory was contacted, no test was executed, no quotation was obtained and no price for a test or a laboratory service was observed. EVD-MC11-414 is a negative record: the DNV page was reachable but its content was not extractable, so no DNV requirement is relied on. No record in this shard supports an IP rating, a temperature rating, an EMC result or any certification.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60945:2002, Edition 4.0, 'Maritime navigation and radiocommunication equipment and systems - General requirements - Methods of testing and required test results'; TC 80; 179 pages; stability date 2028; the 2008 corrigendum is included; the catalogue scope states the requirements apply to shipborne radio equipment, shipborne navigational equipment and, for EMC only, all other bridge-mounted equipment, equipment in close proximity to receiving antennas and equipment capable of interfering with safe navigation of the ship and with radiocommunications; IEC catalogue price CHF 380.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata and scope summary only; the standard text was NOT purchased or read. The CHF 380 is the IEC catalogue price of the document, NOT a quotation for MAREA and not a test cost. The scope statement is not a determination that IEC 60945 applies to a recreational-craft accessory; that determination is made explicitly in D17 section 2.2 as NOT a legal requirement on the recorded market position.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60529:1989+AMD1:1999+AMD2:2013 CSV (Edition 2.2), 'Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)'; TC 70; applies to the classification of degrees of protection provided by enclosures for electrical equipment with a rated voltage not exceeding 72.5 kV; 207 pages; stability date 2027; IEC catalogue price CHF 515.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. This record establishes the existence and classification purpose of the IP Code, NOT any MAREA rating. No IP digit is chosen and no IP claim is made; an IP test of an empty purchased enclosure does not establish the rating of an assembled product, and the IP Code does not address internal condensation.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-52:2017, Edition 3.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-52: Tests - Test Kb: Salt mist, cyclic (sodium chloride solution)'; TC 104; 16 pages; the catalogue description states the test applies to components or equipment designed to withstand a salt-laden atmosphere, has been harmonised with ISO 9227 as far as possible, and adds test methods 7 and 8; IEC catalogue price CHF 80.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read and no severity was selected. Naming the method is not a corrosion qualification and not a claim that any MAREA enclosure would pass.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-6:2007, Edition 7.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-6: Tests - Test Fc: Vibration (sinusoidal)'; TC 104; 82 pages; the catalogue description states it provides a standard procedure to determine the ability of specimens to withstand specified severities of sinusoidal vibration, for mechanical weakness/degradation and to decide acceptability in conjunction with the relevant specification; IEC catalogue price CHF 295.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read, no severity or fixture was defined and no vibration qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-27:2008, Edition 4.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-27: Tests - Test Ea and guidance: Shock'; TC 104; 75 pages; the catalogue description states it provides a standard procedure for determining the ability of a specimen to withstand specified severities of non-repetitive or repetitive shocks using prescribed pulse shapes; IEC catalogue price CHF 260.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read, no pulse severity was selected and no shock qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-30:2005, Edition 3.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-30: Tests - Test Db: Damp heat, cyclic (12 h + 12 h cycle)'; TC 104; 27 pages; the catalogue page states this edition was withdrawn on 2025-08-07 and that IEC 60068-2-30:2025 (Edition 4.0) replaced it; the description covers high humidity combined with cyclic temperature changes producing condensation on the specimen surface; IEC catalogue price CHF 80.
evidence.limitations: The 2005 edition is superseded; the 2025 edition was NOT retrieved or read. No damp-heat severity was selected and no condensation qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 61000-4-2:2008, Edition 2.0, 'Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) - Part 4-2: Testing and measurement techniques - Electrostatic discharge immunity test'; TC 77/SC 77B; 129 pages; the catalogue description covers immunity requirements and test methods for equipment subjected to static electricity discharges from operators directly and from personnel to adjacent objects, defines test levels and procedures; the page states this edition was withdrawn on 2025-03-07 and that IEC 61000-4-2:2025 replaced it; IEC catalogue price CHF 380.
evidence.limitations: The 2008 edition is superseded; the 2025 edition was NOT retrieved or read. No ESD level was selected and no ESD test exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 61000-4-5:2014+AMD1:2017 CSV (Edition 3.1), 'Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) - Part 4-5: Testing and measurement techniques - Surge immunity test'; TC 77/SC 77B; 334 pages; the catalogue description states it relates to immunity requirements, test methods and recommended test levels for unidirectional surges caused by over-voltages from switching and lightning transients and that direct lightning strikes are not covered; IEC catalogue price CHF 680.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. The standard explicitly does not cover direct lightning strikes. No surge level was selected and no transient qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 61000-4-29:2026, Edition 2.0, 'Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) - Part 4-29: Testing and measurement techniques - Voltage dips, short interruptions and voltage variations on d.c. input power port immunity tests'; TC 77/SC 77A; 24 pages; the catalogue description defines test levels, generator, set-up and procedure for DC input power ports connected to low-voltage DC networks external to the equipment, and states ripple is covered by IEC 61000-4-17, not by this document; IEC catalogue price CHF 160.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read, the edition is newly published (2026-07-30) and no DC dip severity was selected. No power-interruption qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: CISPR 32:2015+AMD1:2019 CSV (Edition 2.1), 'Electromagnetic compatibility of multimedia equipment - Emission requirements'; applies to multimedia equipment with a rated r.m.s. AC or DC supply voltage not exceeding 600 V; covers Class A and Class B; frequency range 9 kHz to 400 GHz; the catalogue page states Edition 3.0 is under development (forecast publication 2027-01-01); IEC catalogue price CHF 1230.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. Class A vs Class B is a conformity decision, not chosen here. No emission test exists and no emission result is claimed.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 61162-1:2000, Edition 2.0, 'Maritime navigation and radiocommunication equipment and systems - Digital interfaces - Part 1: Single talker and multiple listeners'; closely aligned with NMEA 0183 version 2.30; the catalogue page states this edition was withdrawn on 2007-04-11 and that a more recent IEC 61162-1:2024 (Edition 6) exists; IEC catalogue price CHF 380.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. This is an interface/digital-communication standard, NOT an environmental or RF qualification standard; it is not used in D17 to derive any environmental severity.

evidence.supportedAssertion: ISO 9227:2022 (Edition 5), 'Corrosion tests in artificial atmospheres - Salt spray tests'; ISO/TC 156; 23 pages; published 2022-11; specifies the neutral salt spray (NSS), acetic acid salt spray (AASS) and copper-accelerated acetic acid salt spray (CASS) apparatus, reagents and procedure; the abstract explicitly states the methods are not intended for comparative ranking of materials or for predicting long-term corrosion resistance; Amendment 1:2024 exists.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only; the standard text was NOT read. The standard itself warns against predicting long-term corrosion resistance, so a pass cannot be extrapolated into a service-life claim.

evidence.supportedAssertion: ISO 4892-2:2013 (Edition 3), 'Plastics - Methods of exposure to laboratory light sources - Part 2: Xenon-arc lamps'; ISO/TC 61/SC 6; 13 pages; published 2013-03; specifies methods for exposing specimens to xenon-arc light in the presence of moisture to reproduce weathering effects; status 'to be revised'; Amendment 1:2021 (classification of daylight filters) exists.
evidence.limitations: Abstract only; the standard text was NOT read. This is a materials-exposure method, not an equipment-level environmental test; it cannot by itself qualify an assembled product.

evidence.supportedAssertion: Requested on 2026-11-02: the DNV rules server returned HTTP 200, but the extracted body contained only cover/trademark text ('The trademarks DNV GL, DNV, the Horizon Graphic and Det Norske Veritas are the properties of companies in the Det Norske Veritas group... WHEN TRUST MATTERS'). The environmental test scope, categories, severities and tables of DNV-CG-0339:2021 were NOT retrievable in this environment.
evidence.limitations: PARTIALLY_INACCESSIBLE: this record is evidence that the source could NOT be read, not evidence of its content. No DNV requirement, severity or category is quoted, adopted or relied on anywhere in D15-D18. Recorded so the auditor does not assume the document was studied.

evidence.publisher: European Commission (DG Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs)
evidence.supportedAssertion: The EMC Directive is Directive 2014/30/EU, published in OJ L 96/79 of 29 March 2014 and repealing Directive 2004/108/EC from 20 April 2016; equipment (apparatus and fixed installations) needs to comply with EMC requirements when placed on the market and/or taken into service; harmonised standards published in the OJEU provide a presumption of conformity; the page states that CE marking can only be affixed after testing the product and performing the conformity assessment procedure prescribed by the applicable EU harmonisation legislation, and that voluntary/unregulated certificates are not a recognised means to prove compliance.
evidence.limitations: Official Commission guidance page; not the legal text itself and not legal advice. It does not determine MAREA's per-configuration applicability (owned by D24) and does not establish any test result.

evidence.publisher: European Commission (DG Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs)
evidence.supportedAssertion: The Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU establishes essential requirements for safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility and efficient use of the radio spectrum; it entered into force on 2014-06-11 and applies from 2016-06-13; the page records that the RED cybersecurity Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 was repealed by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339, published in the OJ on 2026-04-29, with the repeal effective from 2027-12-11 when the CRA takes over, and that the CRA main obligations apply from 2027-12-11.
evidence.limitations: Official Commission guidance page; not the legal text and not legal advice. It does not establish that a MAREA configuration is radio equipment (owned by D24) and does not constitute a test result.

evidence.publisher: European Commission (DG Communications Networks, Content and Technology)
evidence.supportedAssertion: The Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) entered into force on 2024-12-10; its main obligations apply from 2027-12-11 and the reporting obligations apply from 2026-09-11; products bear the CE marking; manufacturers must handle vulnerabilities during the lifecycle; the Commission published practical guidance on 2026-07-27; the page was last updated 2026-09-07.
evidence.limitations: Official Commission policy page; not the regulation text and not legal advice. It does not determine whether a specific MAREA configuration is in scope (owned by D24/D27).

evidence.supportedAssertion: Lloyd's Register Type Approval Test Specification 1 is the 'Performance and Environmental Test Specification' for electrical equipment, control and monitoring equipment, instrumentation and internal communication equipment and programmable electronic systems used in the marine environment; the page states the specification applies to LR Type Approval of those systems for marine use, that the introduction specifies categories of approval for differing environmental conditions together with applicable tests in tabular form, and that it was published in July 2024.
evidence.limitations: Classification-society type-approval framework for classed vessels; it is not an ISO/IEC standard and is NOT applicable to an unclassed recreational craft by default. The specification document itself was NOT retrieved or read. Naming it is a voluntary-reference note, not a compliance claim and not a test result.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex)
evidence.supportedAssertion: EUR-Lex summary of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act): manufacturers must provide security updates during the product's support period, which needs to reflect the period the product is expected to be in use; updates must address vulnerabilities and ensure continued security; the regulation excludes from scope, among others, marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU; importers must verify manufacturer compliance and distributors must ensure CE marking and user information before making products available.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex SUMMARY, not the consolidated regulation text. The summary's application-date fields rendered blank in the retrieved extract, so no date is taken from this record (dates are taken from EVD-MC11-417). The MED exclusion does not by itself remove the CRA from a recreational-craft product, because the MED is not applicable on the recorded market position (HARDWARE-COMPLIANCE-MATRIX.md C-09); the per-configuration determination is owned by D24/D27.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-14:2023, Edition 7.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-14: Tests - Test N: Change of temperature'; TC 104; 70 pages; the catalogue description states it provides tests with specified ambient temperature changes to analyse their impacts on specimens and updates severities, tolerances and test-report requirements; IEC catalogue price CHF 260.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read, no temperature range or rate of change was selected and no thermal-cycling qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-78:2025, Edition 3.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-78: Tests - Test Cab: Damp heat, steady state'; TC 104; 13 pages; the catalogue description covers high humidity at constant temperature WITHOUT condensation over a specified period and applies to small and large, heat-dissipating and non-heat-dissipating specimens; IEC catalogue price CHF 80.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. The method explicitly targets non-condensing humidity, so it does not replace a condensation test. No humidity severity was selected and no humidity qualification exists.

evidence.supportedAssertion: IEC 60068-2-5:2018, Edition 3.0, 'Environmental testing - Part 2-5: Tests - Test S: Simulated solar radiation at ground level and guidance for solar radiation testing and weathering'; TC 104; 54 pages; the catalogue description states it specifies methods for testing equipment or components under simulated solar radiation at the earth's surface and retains Test method Sa (thermal effect) while adding Test method Sb (weathering); IEC catalogue price CHF 272.
evidence.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; the standard text was NOT read. No solar-irradiance profile or exposure duration was selected and no UV/solar qualification exists.

evidence.publisher: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) / International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC)
evidence.supportedAssertion: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (Edition 3) is the international standard for testing and calibration laboratories; it sets out requirements for competence, impartiality and consistent operation, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of testing and calibration results; accreditation bodies use ISO/IEC 17025 as the criteria for assessing and accrediting laboratories; published 2017-11 with a corrected version in 2018-03.
evidence.limitations: Abstract and overview only; the standard text was NOT read. This record establishes the basis on which an 'accredited laboratory' should be judged; it does NOT establish that any specific laboratory is accredited, and no laboratory was contacted or verified.
